simple.meaning: צָעַר (tsâʻar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be small , i.e. (figuratively) ignoble.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Job, Jeremiah, Zechariah, beginning at Job 14:21. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָעַר (H6819) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צָעַר (tsâʻar) / H6819 is traced through Job 14:21, Jeremiah 30:19, Zechariah 13:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.usage: be brought low, little one, be small.
definitions.full: H6819. tsaar [ צָעַר ] verb be, or grow, insignificant (|| זער ; Late Hebrew id. , Assyrian ƒe—êru , be small , Arabic id. ; Syriac be insignificant, despicable ; צְעַר ᵑ7 transitive despise, revile ; — Qal Imperfect (opposed to כָּבֵד ), 3 masculine plural יִצְעֲרוּ Job 14:21 , יִצְעָ֑רוּ Jer 30:19 ; Participle as substantive הַצֹּעֲרִים Zech 13:7 (i.e. sheep, in figure, compare Now).
